portName: Santorini (Thira) – Fira Old Port tender landing and Athinios
seoTitle: Santorini cruise port guide: tenders, cable car, Oia bus
seoDescription: Santorini is a tender port. Cable car to Fira €10 each way (2025), bus to Oia about 25 min, up to €20 Greek cruise fee. Leave Fira 2.5 hrs before all-aboard.
quickAnswer: Santorini is a tender port: ships anchor in the caldera and most passengers are tendered to the Old Port below Fira, with up to 30% landed at Athinios, mainly ship tour groups. From the Old Port take the cable car (€10 adult one way, 2025) or climb about 560–600 steps to Fira. On busy days be back at the top cable car station 2.5 hours before all-aboard, because the queue down can take an hour or more.
intro: Santorini is the one Greek island where the logistics decide your day. Your ship anchors inside a flooded volcanic crater, a tender takes you to a narrow quay at the foot of a 220 m cliff, and the only ways up are a six-seat cable car, a long stepped path or a donkey. Since 31 May 2026 the island's Port Fund sends most cruise passengers through the Old Port and caps Athinios at 30%, so expect the cable car queue to be the main constraint, both up in the morning and down in the afternoon. Plan around it and the rest is simple: Fira is on the cliff edge, Oia is a 25-minute bus ride north, and the island caps cruise visitors at 8,000 a day.
tenderNotes: All cruise ships anchor in the caldera; there is no cruise berth. Tenders are run by the local boatmen and land at the Old Port (Ormos Firon, also called Fira Skala) below Fira. Since 31 May 2026 the Municipal Port Fund requires that no more than 30% of a ship's passengers land at Athinios, the island's ferry port 20–25 minutes by road south of Fira; Athinios is mainly used for ship coach tours. Your ship's daily programme says where your tender lands. When the Karavolades steps were closed after a wall collapse on 27 July 2026, all organised tours were moved to Athinios; the steps reopened in early August 2026 and the 30% cap was restored. Tickets for the tender are issued on board; independent passengers usually go after the tour groups, so expect a wait of 30–60 minutes for an early tender on a busy day.

terminals.name: Old Port (Ormos Firon / Fira Skala) tender landing
terminals.notes: About 220 m below Fira. Linked to Fira by the cable car (3–5 minutes) or the Karavolades steps. No road access for buses. Most independent passengers land here.

terminals.name: Athinios port
terminals.notes: The island's ferry port, south of Fira on the caldera road. Up to 30% of a ship's passengers may land here, mostly on ship tours whose coaches wait at the quay. KTEL buses to Fira are timed to ferries, not cruise tenders.

walkability.detail: From the Old Port you can walk up the Karavolades steps to Fira: about 560–600 wide stone steps with a 220 m climb, no shade and donkey traffic and dung on the path. Fit walkers take 30–45 minutes up; allow 20–30 minutes down. Once in Fira, the town, the caldera path to Firostefani and Imerovigli and the bus station are all on foot. Oia is about 10 km away and needs a bus or taxi.

transportSections.cost: €10 adult, €5 child, €5 per luggage item, one way (2025)
transportSections.detail: Six-seat gondolas, about 600 passengers per hour in each direction. Tickets are sold at the stations only and cannot be bought in advance. Pay at the kiosk before joining the line. The queue down in the afternoon is the main risk of the day when several ships are in.
Starts beside the cable car at the Old Port. Wear shoes with grip; the stones are polished smooth and slippery. Go up early before the heat or come down this way if the cable car queue is too long.

transportSections.mode: Donkey or mule up the steps
transportSections.detail: Greek law bars riders over 100 kg and loads over one fifth of the animal's body weight, and sick, injured or pregnant animals may not work. Welfare groups ask visitors not to ride. If you walk, keep to the wall side when animals pass.

Departs from the Fira bus station, a 10-minute walk from the top cable car station. Every 30 minutes in summer. Pay the conductor on board. Queues build mid-morning and late afternoon; buses fill and you may wait for the next one.

transportSections.mode: KTEL bus Fira – beaches and Akrotiri
transportSections.detail: All routes start from Fira bus station. Akrotiri runs only every 60–90 minutes, so check the printed timetable at the station before you go.
Santorini has very few licensed taxis, and they are hard to find on cruise days. The rank is near the Fira bus station. Do not rely on a taxi for your return.

returnTiming.rule: Be at the top cable car station in Fira by 15:00 for a 17:30 all-aboard (2.5 hours before), earlier if four or more ships are in.
returnTiming.detail: The cable car moves about 600 people an hour downhill. With several ships anchored, the afternoon line can take an hour or more, then you queue again for your ship's tender. Leave Oia by 14:00 at the latest: the bus takes 25 minutes but you may not get on the first one, and you then walk 10 minutes to the cable car.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If the cable car line is too long, walk down the steps (20–30 minutes). Tell the tender staff at the Old Port your ship's name; tenders run until the last tender time printed in your daily programme. If you landed at Athinios, a taxi from Fira takes 20–25 minutes but taxis are scarce, so ask your ship's port agent (number on the daily programme) for help early.

diyVsExcursion.item: Getting from the tender to Fira and back
diyVsExcursion.ship: Ship tours often land at Athinios and use coaches, skipping the cable car queue
diyVsExcursion.diy: €20 cable car up and down (2025), or free on the steps
diyVsExcursion.saving: Depends on your line's tour price

diyVsExcursion.ship: Guided tour; price varies by line
diyVsExcursion.saving: Depends on your line's tour price

excursionAdvice: This is one of the few ports where a ship tour can make sense for practical reasons. Tour groups are tendered first and, when they land at Athinios, avoid the cable car queue entirely. If you want both Oia and Akrotiri, or you have limited mobility, the ship tour removes the main risk of the day. If you only want Fira and Oia and you are on an early tender, doing it yourself by cable car and bus is simple and much cheaper.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes anchoring at 07:00, first tenders from 07:30, landing at the Old Port and a busy day with three or more ships. Last tender usually 30 minutes before all-aboard.

steps.what: Collect a tender ticket as early as possible and land at the Old Port.
Buy a cable car ticket and ride up, or walk the steps while it is cool.
Walk 10 minutes to Fira bus station and take the bus to Oia.
Walk Oia's main lane to the castle viewpoint and down towards the windmills before the coach groups peak.
Lunch in Oia or take the bus back and eat in Fira.
Back in Fira. Walk the caldera path north to Firostefani for views, or visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (closed Tuesday).
Join the downhill cable car queue. If it is very long, walk down the steps.
Board a tender at the Old Port and be on board by 16:00, 90 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Oia
sights.why: The village at the northern tip, with white houses and blue domes stacked on the caldera rim. The views towards Fira and the windmills are the reason most people come.
sights.tip: Go in the morning. Sunset is usually after your all-aboard time and is the most crowded hour of the day.

sights.name: Fira caldera path to Firostefani and Imerovigli
sights.why: A paved path along the cliff edge with the best views of the caldera and your anchored ship.
sights.tip: Firostefani is 15–20 minutes from Fira; Imerovigli and Skaros Rock add another 20–30 minutes each way.

sights.name: Museum of Prehistoric Thera, Fira
sights.why: Wall paintings and finds from Akrotiri, the Bronze Age town buried by the eruption. Air-conditioned and close to the bus station.
sights.tip: Open 08:30–15:30 and closed on Tuesdays in the 2025 schedule.

sights.name: Akrotiri archaeological site
sights.why: A Bronze Age town preserved under volcanic ash, now under a large roof. The most important ancient site on the island.
sights.tip: Buses from Fira run every 60–90 minutes. Check the return times at the stop before you go in.

sights.name: Archaeological Museum of Thera, Fira
sights.why: Finds from Ancient Thera and other Greek and Roman sites on the island. Near the top cable car station.
sights.tip: Closed on Mondays in the 2025 schedule.

sights.name: Orthodox Metropolitan Cathedral, Fira
sights.why: The large cathedral in the centre of Fira with an open courtyard and painted interior.

sights.name: Ancient Thera
sights.why: Ruins of the Hellenistic and Roman town on Mesa Vouno ridge above Kamari, with views over both coasts.
sights.tip: The road up is steep and there is no direct bus from Fira; only for a long call. Closed Wednesdays in the 2025 schedule.

beaches.name: Kamari
beaches.note: Long black sand and pebble beach with sunbeds and tavernas. The sand gets very hot.

beaches.name: Perissa / Perivolos
beaches.note: Black sand, sunbeds, calm water. Buses every 30–45 minutes.

beaches.name: Red Beach (Akrotiri)
beaches.howToGetThere: KTEL bus from Fira to Akrotiri, then a short walk to the viewpoint
beaches.note: Known for its red cliffs. The cliffs are unstable and rockfall warnings are posted; view it from above rather than sitting under the cliff.

food.dish: Tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters) and fava (yellow split pea purée)
food.where: Tavernas in Fira and Oia; both dishes are on most menus on the island

food.dish: Assyrtiko white wine tasting with caldera view
food.where: Santo Wines, Pyrgos (between Fira and Athinios)
Ammoudi Bay below Oia (about 300 steps down from Oia)

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving the cable car until the last hour
commonMistakes.fix: Join the downhill queue 2.5 hours before all-aboard on busy days, or walk down.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning to see the Oia sunset
commonMistakes.fix: Check your all-aboard time. Most cruise calls end before sunset; see Oia in the morning.
The island has very few taxis. Use the KTEL bus and leave buffer time.

commonMistakes.mistake: Walking the steps in sandals at midday
commonMistakes.fix: Wear shoes with grip and walk early or late. The stones are slippery and there is no shade.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming you land where you did last time
commonMistakes.fix: Read the daily programme. Since May 2026 most passengers land at the Old Port, but tour groups may land at Athinios.

commonMistakes.mistake: Being surprised by the cruise fee
commonMistakes.fix: Greece charges a per-port cruise passenger fee: up to €20 in Santorini from June to September and €12 in October (2026). Your line adds it to your account or includes it in the fare.

safety: Santorini has low street crime. The main risks are physical: heat and sun on the exposed caldera path, slippery stone steps, and walking close to unfenced cliff edges for photos. The island had an earthquake swarm in early 2025; follow any closures and signs, and note the location of your ship's tender point in case of an alert. Carry water. Watch your bag in the crowds at the cable car and Oia's main lane.
scams: Unlicensed drivers offering rides at the Fira bus station or Old Port at inflated prices. Use the KTEL bus or a licensed taxi and agree the fare first.
Donkey handlers quoting one price at the bottom and asking for more at the top. Agree the full price before you get on, or walk.
Restaurants on the caldera edge with no prices on the menu. Ask for a printed menu with prices before ordering.
accessibility: Santorini is hard for wheelchair users on a cruise day. Tenders involve steps from the ship's platform into a moving boat, and the crew decides on the day whether a wheelchair user can transfer. At the Old Port the cable car is the only route without steps, but boarding the moving gondolas can be difficult and the Fira streets are steep and stepped. A ship tour landing at Athinios, with a coach, is usually the most practical option. Oia's main lane is paved and flat in parts, but side lanes are stepped.
rainyDay: Rain is rare from May to September. On a wet or very windy day, tenders may be suspended and the call cancelled. If you get ashore, the Museum of Prehistoric Thera and the Archaeological Museum of Thera in Fira are both close to the cable car and indoors. The steps become very slippery when wet; use the cable car.
crowdTips: Santorini caps cruise visitors at 8,000 a day under its 2025–2026 berthing policy, but that still means long queues when three or more ships call. The cable car is busiest from 08:00 to 10:00 going up and from 14:00 to 17:00 going down. Oia's main lane and castle viewpoint are at their worst from late morning and again before sunset. Fira's caldera path is quieter north of Firostefani. Check a cruise schedule for your date to see how many ships are in.

faqs.a: Yes. All cruise ships anchor in the caldera. Most passengers are tendered to the Old Port below Fira; up to 30% may land at Athinios, mainly on ship tours.

faqs.q: How do I get from the Santorini cruise port to Fira?
faqs.a: From the Old Port take the cable car (€10 adult one way, 2025, 3–5 minutes plus queue) or walk up about 560–600 steps in 30–45 minutes. From Athinios, ship coaches, KTEL buses or taxis take 20–25 minutes.

faqs.q: How long is the cable car queue in Santorini?
faqs.a: With one or two ships, often 15–30 minutes. With three or more, an hour or more is common, especially going down in the afternoon.

faqs.q: How do I get from Fira to Oia by bus?
faqs.a: KTEL buses leave Fira bus station about every 30 minutes in summer. The ride takes about 25 minutes and costs €2.20 one way (2026), paid on board.

faqs.q: Should I ride a donkey up from the Old Port?
faqs.a: Greek law bars riders over 100 kg and requires shade, water and rest for the animals. Welfare groups recommend walking or using the cable car instead.

faqs.q: What is the Greek cruise passenger fee for Santorini?
faqs.a: From July 2025, Greece charges each disembarking passenger per port: in Santorini €20 from June to September, €12 in April, May and October and €4 from November to March. Passengers who stay on board pay nothing.

faqs.q: What can I do in Santorini in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Take the cable car to Fira, bus to Oia in the morning, return to Fira for lunch and the caldera path or a museum, and join the downhill cable car queue 2.5 hours before all-aboard.
None within walking distance of the Old Port. Kamari (15 minutes) and Perissa (25 minutes) are reachable by KTEL bus from Fira.
